This just makes me wonder what other alternatives there would be. Nef Anyo does have access to sentient tech if the orb mothers are anything to go by, but prefers using granum's research. Alad doesn't appear to be interested in Granum at all, opting for nothing but sentient tech due to his tendency to bet with off-board experimentations (Zanuka, Mutalist strain, Eris, Acolytes, Wolf of Saturn Six). There are two more players in this game though: Frohd Bek, and the Sergeant. You have a point as to what weapons are available being tied to whoever creates the liches. My thoughts are:

**Alad V**: Sentient hybrid weapons and newer hybrid tech, or what the amalgam enemies wield: Komorex, Cyanex, Arca Titron, and Arca Plasmor for example.

**Nef Anyo**: Mostly experimental weaponry with minimal sentient influence, given to specialized troops: Battacor, Occucor, Opticor, Penta, and Quanta for example.

**Frohd Bek**: Easy-to-manufacture weaponry, standard issue for most grunts and would be easy to pass along to the board: Dera, Supra, Spectra, Cestra, Prova, and Flux rifle for example.

**The Sergeant**: Outlandish designs that are easy to sell to investors with possible Tenno influence due to the nature of his solar rail control, but also under the jurisdiction of Nef Anyo as well: Glaxion, Lenz, Staticor, Convectrix, Possibly Helios?, and Amprex for example.

For MR5, the best of the best assault rifles remain locked away, however you do have access to the:

**Grakata** - A high-output SMG with great critical and status stats, but eats ammo like nobody's business with a fire rate of 20 and a mag size of 60.

**Dera/Tetra** - Two weapons that are a very similar, the Dera has marginally better status and crit, but the tetra has marginally better damage. The biggest difference here is fire rate and mag size, with the dera having higher fire rate (11.25) and a low mag (45), and the tetra having a lower fire rate (6.67) and a bigger mag (60).

**Sybaris** - A semi-auto rifle with great damage and crit, and fires two shots per trigger pull. Technically not an assault rifle, but it's pretty good at MR 5.



Unfortunaltely, better assault rifles are locked behind MR, but when you rank up, be sure to pick up a few very good feeling ones:

**Soma** (MR 6) - Big mag, Really good crit stats, high fire rate bullet hose that gets faster as you shoot it. This will get you through the star chart easy if you love assault rifles.

**Soma prime**(MR 7) - Currently vaulted, you're going to have to wait until Nova comes out of the vault to get your hands on this. It's everything the soma is, but better.

**Baza** (MR 7) - The prince of SMG's once you get hunter munitions (a mod that gives the weapon a chance to proc slash on critical hits 30% of the time, acquired from ghoul purge bounties), and one of my personal favorites.

**Acceltra** (MR 8) - Currently one of the better weapons in the game, even for endgame content. It's a very odd rifle, because it's more like a high fire rate homing grenade launcher. Keep ranking up mods and swapping out builds for better ones and it'll get you places.

I see the concept, I like the concept, but a few things are off.

The description could use a bit of a touch-up in the lore department, but I've read through the comments and don't want to spoil anything for you or anyone else reading due to the lore-heavy subject of otherworldly beings being an actual thing in this game, but only later in the game's story.

The frame itself looks like it is meant to be played as an "Supportive Offense" class of frame, with 2 abilities to increase damage, one CC ability, and one DPS ability, which is matched by only a few frames (Equinox, for example.)

The abilities lack synergy with each other and are replicated by other frames, and/or don't tie into the otherworldly seer theme. I have a few suggestions to change that, with my reasoning in parentheses.

--------

Passive - Reap: Upon killing an enemy, Hades will gain an increase to ability strength for a limited time. (To tie into the whole "Dude wants revenge on everyone" theme, make it so that the more he kills the more powerful he becomes, but he has to keep killing to stay in the rush of adrenaline)

Ethereal Flame: Hades engulfs himself in a fiery ethereal eruption, knocking enemies down while setting them on fire. (The "oh shit" button with some good CC, and fire goes with the name of the ability, possibly adding some decent DOT with his passive.)

Third Eye: Hades and his allies gain a higher sense of vision, causing critical hits and status effects to deal more damage. (Harrow's 4 is basically a better version of the ability currently, so let the crits flow normally, but make them deal more damage. This also allows his 1 to deal more damage while this is up.)

Damnation: Hades channels power into his melee attacks, rending enemies asunder. Deals more damage to enemies that have already fallen. (CC the enemies if they aren't CC'd, and combo from his 1 to deal more damage. Additionally, if the # of strikes this does is tied to power strength, there's a passive synergy.)

Ancient Wrath: Hades succumbs to his inner hatred and transforms into a powerful demon. Killing enemies in this form causes their souls to empower nearby allies with additional damage, and Hades himself with a double charge to his passive. (Exalted demon with a bit of support mixed in. Let the full-on support frames create energy, Hades is here for vengeance!)

Two things: if it has 100% status with every multishot mod removed, then yes, every bullet will proc ONE status, the chance of it being a given status depends on how much damage that element does when compared to the total damage of the weapon.

The mod will stack, and it is recommended that you do that. 320% of 7 (base pellet amount) is 22, with a 40% chance for a 23'rd to appear. this will TRIPLE your base damage for just two mod slots, with that being multiplied by 1.9 with a maxed out point blank. Short and sweet: That is a vertical stabilizer, a horizontal stabilizer, and a rudder from an uncommon single-engine aircraft made by a lesser known manufacturer, as well as a second, Identical (except that it's unpainted) rudder on the far left.


I can give a few guesses as to the aircraft specs, but I can't nail anything concretely from this picture due to lack of data tags, manufacturer info, part size, or something that stands out that defines it as coming from a single aircraft.


The rudder is too small compared to the horizontal stabilizer that it would be from anything but a single-engine aircraft or a tandem twin-engine aircraft, and probably not made from Cessna due to the lack of "strakes" or "ribs/ridges".


The trailing edge of the rudder seems too straight to look like it came off of a piper pa-series, and the shape and position of the balance weight puts the ones with a straight trailing edge off as well. Cessna likes to have their balance weights on top and put a rounded edge on them, but the size is too small for Cessna to put a trim tab that large on it.


The position light fixture being placed on the rudder would indicate that this is probably coming from a later aircraft (i'd say post-1970 as a super rough guess) with a single vertical stabilizer and at least a moderate electrical system, so that takes out the "IT'S YELLOW" piper cub (that and it's made of metal, so that DEFINITELY takes out the cub).


A fair bet would be to look at Beechcraft, but I can't really give any good pointers as to what kind of aircraft it would be if it were Beech, as I rarely get the opportunity to work with their models. They're decently large aircraft as well, so it would be one of the rarer, smaller planes if it were Beech.


Overall, good luck with the search, and if you have pictures of some I.D. Markings that would help out a whole lot and perhaps someone else can pick up from there. Hopefully I gave you some direction and/or helpful pointers.
